title: Biceps Femoris Long Head Fascicle Length Not Associated With Hamstring Injury Risk in NCAA Football Athletes.
journal: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To determine whether biceps femoris long head (BFlh) fascicle length (FL) is related to hamstring injury (HSI) risk in collegiate football athletes.

sections.label: PARTICIPANTS
sections.text: Division I Collegiate football athletes (n = 129, age = 20.03 ± 1.68 years, body mass index = 29.50 ± 5.06 kg/m2).

sections.label: INTERVENTIONS
sections.text: Biceps femoris long head FL measurements were previously taken on the nondominant leg of each athlete. Presence or absence of HSI for 2 playing seasons and training camps was evaluated through retrospective review of medical records.

sections.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
sections.text: Whether a shorter BFlh FL was associated with increased risk for any HSI.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Biceps femoris long head FL was not associated with HSI risk. Body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 was incidentally found to be protective (odds ratio = 0.27, 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.84, P = 0.03).

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Biceps femoris long head FL is not an ideal measurement for predicting risk of HSI in American football athletes.
